subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
THE RULE. When both allocators replicate ONE value across several registers, the correspondence between our registers and the target's is genuinely MANY-TO-MANY, and no refinement of a function-valued renaming state can express it. verify_consistent_recolor carries a partial function our-reg -> target-reg, so at the definitions it binds root-to-root and then refuses the first later use that reads the other stream's COPY. Read such a refusal as a fact about the checker's STATE SHAPE, not about the function.

THE CURE, and it is a relation. Carry R with the invariant '(a,b) in R => our a and the target's b hold the same value at this program point': seed with the identity at entry (both streams start from one machine state), narrow at every definition (a define retires every (ours,*) and every (*,target) pair, because our register now holds a new value and the target's was overwritten), intersect at joins, and CLOSE OVER VALUE-PRESERVING COPIES in BOTH streams — after `our: d<-s` every target register value-equal to s is value-equal to d, and symmetrically on the target side. Both closure directions are load-bearing: CameraSupervisor needs the target-side one for (f4,f5) and the our-side one for (f31,f30). Because every accepted use is backed by a member of R, the rewritten instruction reads operands holding the values our instruction read, which is exactly what equivalence requires.

THE TRAP THAT KILLS THE OBVIOUS VERSION, measured. The natural first design is a SINGLE-STREAM copy web on our side: at the refusing use, substitute the same-valued register of ours that maps to what the target wants. On CameraSupervisor that is substituting f27 for f4 at +0xc4, and it is UNSOUND: our f27 is redefined inside the loop at +0x13c and +0x16c, so f4 and f27 are not equal on the second iteration. A correct single-stream value numbering therefore refuses the site, and the prototype that tried it produced ZERO usable webs at both refusal offsets. The equality that actually holds is cross-stream and flow-sensitive, which is what the relation encodes and a single-stream web cannot.

A SECOND MECHANISM HIDES BEHIND THE FIRST. Closing the value split on CameraSupervisor immediately exposed two words the relation still refuses: fcmpu with its two operands EXCHANGED between the streams. That is not a value question. Exchanging fcmpu/fcmpo operands swaps FL and FG and leaves FE and FU untouched, so it is equivalence-preserving exactly when every consumer of that CR field reads only EQ or SO and the field is dead at every exit — a CR-BIT LIVENESS proof, refusing any ordering branch, mcrf, mfcr, CR-logical, or a field live at exit. Expect the pair: a schedule residual that produced replicated values often also produced exchanged compare operands.

FAIL-CLOSED SHAPE, because the mode is strictly more permissive than the strict proof. It is opt-in per rule; it never runs unless the strict proof has already failed; it REFUSES if the strict proof succeeds (a stale declaration must be removed, not left resting on the wider mode); it refuses to compose with unproven_recolor_audit or with a post-recolor permutation; and every escape it takes must be DECLARED, with an undeclared escape and a declared-but-never-used escape both errors. So a rule cannot widen silently and a source change that moves the residual fails the build instead of being absorbed.

POPULATION, measured image-wide this run. 2842 equal-size functions, 91 pure register-field candidates, 68 already served by the strict proof, 2 served by this mode (game/game/controls::InitControls, closed; game/pb/dbgtext::fn_800C031C, an already-pinned unproven audit now replaced by the proof), 21 still refused. So the mode is NARROW on the no-permutation population and its value is concentrated in the composed cases — CameraSupervisor needed it on top of two permutation windows. Reproduce with tools/gdl/composed_census/wf_value_equality_census.py.
